title.narrative: 10 Dec 2014 | News Release: https://www.adb.org/news/adb-help-transform-local-economy-baise-prc-through-new-tvet-system
Loan 3215: 100% of contracts awarded and 100% disbursed as of 12 Jan 2024

Progress Toward Outcome: Since the project was declared effective in 6 July 2015, there has been good progress in the implementation arrangements and procurement for the project. The project management office (PMO) staff are in place and the imprest account have been created. All five civil works contracts have been awarded and 3 of 4 consulting packages have been awarded. The first contract for civil works (C02: Student dormitory B1, B2 and B3) under phase II has started in 2015, three contracts have been contracted in 2016 (C01: Site utilities, site development and slope protection; C04: Gym and Sports facilities, and C05: Library, Chemistry and Biology, Physics, Electronic and Math), and contract C03: Business, Political and Law, Art and Education, Administration, Chinese and Foreign language was awarded in 2017. One of the two goods contract (E01) was awarded in 2020 and the last goods contract (E02) was awarded in 2021.
Three consulting contracts have been awarded: (i) CS4: Project Implementation Start-Up Support was awarded to Mr. Yang Ze and mobilized on 30 July 2015; (ii) CS2: Project Implementation Management Support was awarded to Helison Information Consulting Co., Ltd. with contract signed on 30 June 2016 and ADB approval given on 15 July 2016; (iii) CS1: Multilevel TVET Capacity Building and Innovation was awarded to ET Group International Pty. Ltd. with contract signed on 24 October 2016 and ADB approval given on 8 November 2016; (iv) GS1 was awarded to Guangxi Hongxuan Cultural Investment Co., Ltd. With contract signed on 30 November 2020 and ADB approval given on 4 December 2020; and (v) GS2 awarded to Guangxi Kaihe Technology Co., Ltd. With contract signed on 23 November 2020 and ADB approval on 4 December 2020.
The contract closing date was extended to 31 December 2021 for the completion of the procurement of the one remaining goods contract, TVET capacity building activities, and remaining 4 multilevel TVET programs under the project.
Loan inception mission was fielded on 23-27 November 2015 and review missions were fielded on 7-10 February 2017, 13-17 November 2017 (midterm review), 22-23 March 2018, 18-21 September 2018, and 25-28 June 2019. The next review mission will be the project completion review.
Some results are in the Audited Project Financial Statements | Jun 2022: https://www.adb.org/sites/default/files/project-documents/47009/47009-002-apfs-en_3.pdf
Some results are in the Social Monitoring Reports | Jan 2020: https://www.adb.org/sites/default/files/project-documents/47009/47009-002-smr-en_1.pdf

Status of Implementation Progress: 1. The progress of this component has been delayed. The consulting firm for multilevel TVET capacity development and innovation was mobilized in December 2016 and has made limited progress until March 2018. The process of developing standards in consultation with industry has commenced and some preliminary work on new curriculum. Trainings have been organized in 2017.
2. Phase I of Chengbi new campus (domestic funds) have been completed in 2016. More than 7,000 students have moved in and are attending classes. The first ADB funded contract for civil works under phase II (C02: Student dormitory B1, B2 and B3) has started in 2015 and two contracts started in Q2 2016 (C01: Site utilities, site development and slope protection and C04: Gym and sports facilities). The two remaining contracts were awarded in Q2 2017 (C03: Administrative Building, Chinese and Foreign Language Department Building, Business School Building, Political and Law Department Building, Art and Education Science Department Building, and C05: Library, Physics and Electronics, and Math Department Building and Biochemical Building).
3. Delays in TVET consultant selection, changes and problems in consultant leadership and lack of engagement by BU leadership resulted in slow progress for this output. Efforts are underway to engage with local industry to better understand need, and to reflect those needs into the new curriculum.
4. PMO functioning and staffed with 12 people. Imprest account established and request for initial advance submitted to PRCM on 27 Nov 2015.
